title: A release or pre-release could be published from any branch
description:
image-build.yml's publish checks the release version and its notes but not the branch it runs on. A pre-release dispatched from any branch pushed Docker Hub `latest`, and a non-maintenance release from a branch other than main only had to be newer than the newest release to become GitHub's latest, Docker Hub `latest`, apt stable and the docs - all from an unreviewed ref. A collaborator's mistake, or the image factory's workflow-dispatch token (which can dispatch any workflow on any branch), could publish images the fleet trusts from code that never reached main.

**Affected**: the publish pipeline, hence the images every node installs or updates to.

**Fix**: a release or pre-release is refused unless it is dispatched on `refs/heads/main`, and a maintenance release unless on a `refs/heads/release/*` branch, in the early validation before the build.

**Besides updating**: nothing on nodes; the change is in the CI workflow.
